kanban-claude 0.4.0.dev5

kanban wait-ci stops calling a PR failed when CI only cancelled an old run to start a new one. The dispatcher starts no card while the plugin a worker would load is at another version than the daemon. A worker that meets an ambiguous card takes the most reasonable reading, says which, and carries on.

Release explainer, 2026-11-11. Diff v0.4.0.dev4 (7bb3c7d) to 922b52c, the merge of PR #25. This is a pre-release. The version bump to 0.4.0.dev5, the changelog heading and the releases row come after the diff and are not part of it.

  • 15 of 60

    recent PRs of one board repo carry a cancelled check next to an all-green set: a run that CI cancelled to start its replacement

  • 2 of 2

    Claude accounts on the machine these changes were measured on had the plugin one release ahead of the daemon, with nothing saying so to the board

  • 3

    merged PRs, #23, #24 and #25, with 4 commits; +189 and −22 lines in 12 files

    test functions; no new config key, no schema change, 1138 tests green

Background

Where these changes came from

A review of the plugin on three live boards looked for places where a run did the right work and the board still read it wrong. Three turned up. Each is a signal that meant something other than what the code took it to mean.

  • A cancel that was read as a failure. A workflow with a concurrency group and cancel-in-progress cancels its older run when a second trigger starts one on the same head commit. Until the newer run registers its own check, gh pr checks still lists the cancelled run's check, in the fail bucket. One recorded run on a live board ended this way: kanban wait-ci answered failed: <check> for a run that had only been cancelled and replaced. The state ends when the new run registers its check, so a later look at the PR shows nothing wrong.
  • Two versions that drifted apart in silence. A worker is started as claude --agent kanban-claude:<role> with no plugin path, so it loads the roles, skills and rules of whatever version its Claude account has installed. The daemon, the CLI and the protocol stay at the version /kanban-claude:setup last installed. After a plugin update without setup, role text written for one CLI ran against another. The session-start line said so to whoever opened a session; the board itself kept dispatching.
  • A question nobody was there to answer. A dispatched run has no reader. A worker that blocked with needs_input over an ambiguity a person would have settled in a sentence left the card parked until the owner came by.

PR #23 carries the rule for ambiguous cards, PR #24 the CI fix and PR #25 the version hold. Line numbers are in the files at the head of this diff.

Walkthrough

Three changes, one at a time

Each area says what changed, why, and how you notice it as the operator.

A cancelled run is judged by the run that replaced it !fixed+added

What changed
PR #24. worker._poll now asks gh pr checks for name,bucket,link. When a check in the fail or cancel bucket links to an Actions run (/actions/runs/<id>), it lists the workflow runs of the head commit (_head_runs: gh pr view --json headRefOid, then gh run list --commit). _replaced maps each run whose conclusion is cancelled to the bucket of the newest run with the same workflow name and event, when that newest run is a different run and was not cancelled itself: pending while it runs, then pass or fail. The check takes that bucket. The path for a PR with no checks yet (_runs) drops the replaced runs before it folds the rest.

What stays failed. A run that failed by itself, even with a newer run queued behind it. A cancelled run that nothing replaced, which is a cancel by hand. A replacement that was cancelled too. A check with no Actions link, such as an external status: no extra gh call is made for it.
Why
A cancel says nothing about the code. The bucket could not tell the two cases apart, since gh files such a check under fail; the run behind the check can. The builder otherwise spends a run looking for a failure that is not there, and the reviewer gets a card whose summary says CI failed.
How you notice it
kanban wait-ci answers pending where it answered failed: <check>, then the real result. test_worker.py covers both buckets, the four cases that must stay failed, and the no-checks path. Run against three real PRs with this history, the lookup mapped each cancelled run to pass.

No card starts while the plugin and the daemon differ +added~changed

What changed
PR #25. runner.plugin_mismatch(config_dir) reads plugins/installed_plugins.json in a Claude config directory and returns an installed version of kanban-claude when none of its installs is the runtime's own version. dispatcher.skip_reason calls it for the board's account, after the login pause and the quota wall, and skips the card with plugin_mismatch:<version>. The check runs on every tick, so the hold lifts on the first tick after the versions match; nothing is stored and nothing needs kanban resume.

It fails open. A missing or unreadable listing, an account that lists no install (a --plugin-dir checkout), and one install at the daemon's version among several are not held. Running cards finish.

The words around it. The session-start line for a version difference now says that the daemon starts no card on an account whose plugin differs from it. The kanban skill has a row for the skip, and the README's upgrade paragraph describes the hold.
Why
A hold is cheaper than a mixed run. New role text against an old CLI fails in ways that look like the card's fault: a verb the CLI does not have, an exit code the prompt does not expect. One daemon serves boards on more than one account, so the check is per account, not per machine.
How you notice it
The card's event log in kanban show carries skipped with plugin_mismatch:<version>, and kanban dispatch --dry-run prints the same reason. Update the plugin in that account, run /kanban-claude:setup, and the cards start by themselves.

A worker settles an ambiguous card alone ~changed

What changed
PR #23. prompts/rules.md, which every dispatched role reads, now says that nobody is watching the run: when what the card asks for is ambiguous, take the most reasonable reading, state it at the top of the summary (and of the PR body, if one is opened), and carry on. Blocking with needs_input over such an ambiguity is kept for a choice that cannot be undone and could reasonably go either way, after the preparation is done, with the decision and a proposed default in the reason. agents/scout.md drops its own rule to block on an ambiguous question and answers the most reasonable reading instead.
Why
A block costs the owner a round trip and the card its place in the flow. A stated reading costs one line and can be corrected in review. The needs_input cases the roles and the rules name stay as they were: the change is scoped to ambiguity in what the card asks.
How you notice it
Fewer cards parked on a question, and a first line in the summary that names the reading taken. If the reading is wrong, send the card back with the right one.

Known limits

What this release does not do

  • The cancel window was not caught live. The failing state was replayed from recorded gh output and the run lookup was run against real PRs, but the patched wait-ci has not yet met a check in that state on a live PR.
  • A failed lookup waits instead of failing. If gh pr view or gh run list errors while a check is failing, that poll answers pending and the next one asks again. A real failure is then reported at the next poll that gets through, not at once.
  • gh run list returns 20 runs. On a head commit with more runs than that, a replacement can fall outside the listing. The cancelled run then stays failed, which is the old behaviour.
  • The hold compares version strings. Commits that land under an unchanged version are invisible to it. It catches a plugin update without setup, not a stale checkout.
  • One matching install counts as a match. An account can hold a user install and a project install at different versions, and which one a worker loads is not known to the dispatcher. A stale project install can slip through. The code marks this with a shortcut: comment.
  • The hold is quiet for a watcher. It is a skipped event, which kanban watch --actionable does not print. The session-start line and kanban show do.

Upgrade notes

Moving from 0.4.0.dev4 to 0.4.0.dev5

  1. Update the plugin in every Claude account your boards run on (/plugin update), then run /kanban-claude:setup between cards so the daemon and the CLI move with it. The schema stays at 7: no migration, no backup.
  2. An account left on 0.4.0.dev4 holds its boards. Its cards wait with plugin_mismatch:0.4.0.dev4 until that account is updated. This is the new hold doing its job; nothing is lost and nothing needs kanban resume.
  3. Between the plugin update and setup, a new session prints that cards are held. The daemon still running at that point is 0.4.0.dev4 or older and has no hold, so it keeps starting cards until setup replaces it.
  4. There is no new config key and no new verb. kanban wait-ci keeps its exit codes.

Range covered

  • 1ad8a0e judge a cancelled run by the run that replaced it (PR #24)
  • 7163216 hold cards while the account's plugin differs from the daemon (PR #25)

No PR had a merge conflict. The version bump, the changelog heading and the releases row come after the range.

Quiz

Check what you took from this page

Four questions. Pick an answer to see the explanation.

1. A check sits in the fail bucket and links to a run that was cancelled. A newer run of the same workflow and event is queued on the same head. What does kanban wait-ci answer?

The first answer is what 0.4.0.dev4 did. A cancel says nothing about the code, so the check takes the bucket of the run that replaced it, and that run is still pending. It is not a pass either: if the newer run fails, the check fails.

2. The same check, but the run behind it ended with failure, and a newer run is queued. What now?

A run that failed by itself tested the head and found something. A later run does not unsay that. The same holds for a cancelled run with no successor, and for a successor that was cancelled too.

3. You update the plugin in one account and do not run setup. Under 0.4.0.dev5, what happens to that account's ready cards?

The hold is per account and checked on every tick, so it needs no resume and does not touch boards on an account that still matches. Running cards finish on the code they started with.

4. A card can be read two ways, and either reading can be corrected in review. What does the worker do?

Nobody is watching the run, so a question waits until the owner comes by. Blocking is kept for a choice that cannot be undone and could reasonably go either way, after the preparation is done.
